claims.claim_text: DDP allocates import clearance, duties and applicable taxes to seller, with delivery at named point ready for unloading.
claims.publication_or_revision_date: Opened DDP explanation and obligations; commercial delivery allocation.
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: ICC explains commercial delivery point and clearance/cost allocation.
claims.caveat: Not a local customs-registration rule; exceptions require contractual analysis.

claims.claim_text: ICC cautions seller unable to arrange import clearance to consider DAP or DPU.
claims.publication_or_revision_date: Opened DDP explanation and obligations; commercial delivery allocation.
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: ICC identifies alternative terms where import clearance is left to buyer.
claims.caveat: Does not imply those alternatives fit every purchase.

claims.claim_text: Incoterm choice does not restrict use of customs valuation methods.
claims.publication_or_revision_date: Updated 14 April 2026; trade terms do not determine customs valuation method.
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: HMRC says DDP can still use method 1 and describes trade-term role.
claims.geographic_scope: UK HMRC customs-valuation guidance, updated 14 April 2026
claims.caveat: No specific valuation result given for a shipment.

claims.claim_text: US entry statute assigns reasonable-care entry responsibilities and identifies eligible importer-of-record parties.
claims.publication_or_revision_date: 2024 published Code edition; US entry responsibilities and eligible parties.
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: Published code describes entry information and eligible filing parties.
claims.caveat: Not represented as a worldwide rule. Current transaction-specific eligibility requires broker/legal review.

claims.claim_text: UK direct and indirect customs representation have different liability consequences; appointment does not remove due diligence.
claims.source_title: Appointing someone to deal with customs
claims.publication_or_revision_date: Updated 21 August 2024; direct and indirect representation.
claims.page_or_section: Decide how they act; direct/indirect sections; lines 93,151–186
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: HMRC distinguishes agent acting in principal name from own name on behalf of principal.
claims.geographic_scope: UK guidance; article specifically discusses Great Britain and flags Northern Ireland separately
claims.caveat: No blanket assertion that a broker becomes importer or that all liabilities transfer.

claims.claim_text: Paying import VAT/holding certificate alone does not establish deduction entitlement.
claims.publication_or_revision_date: Ownership, importer role and import-VAT deduction in the described UK contexts.
claims.page_or_section: VIT44400, ownership and toll-operator passages; lines 73–88
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: HMRC discusses ownership, importer role and incorrect deductions by non-owners.
claims.geographic_scope: Specific UK input-tax contexts; updated manual 4 June 2026
claims.caveat: Not tax advice or a universal VAT-recovery entitlement.

claims.claim_text: Obtain importer identities, representation, funding and records before shipment.
claims.page_or_section: Ask for names; Turn delivered price into usable order
claims.supporting_passage_paraphrase: Editorial due-diligence questions synthesizing commercial and legal distinctions.
claims.caveat: No tax rate, bond amount, filing deadline or regulatory exemption invented.

limits: No invented project, quotation, numerical example or customer result. Primary source statements are attributed; proposed workflow is editorial advice.
